answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to locked collateral recorded in a shared atlas. Random audits arrive like a zephyr: the protocol selects agents without warning and demands a fresh signature from the key that owns the stake; a missed check slashes the deposit and deletes the identity. Because every clone must post its own bond, a Sybil attacker pays linearly per fake agent instead of once, so buying a tenth of the vote costs ten stakes. Honest agents earn a velvet yield on their lock, while the attacker's capital sits idle and gets forfeited.
